newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt trade brisk, junk issues up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt trade brisk, junk issues up.

text.p: The U.S. corporate debt market enjoyed brisk trade centered on fresh investment-grade issuance, traders said, with spreads marginally wider in spots at mid-session.

A frenzy for higher yields lifted the bid for new junk paper more than one point, high-yield sources said. Investment grade issuance began to pressure spreads, some said, but prices held remarkably well when deals were freed to trade.
Reflecting one niche, Sears, Roebuck Acceptance Corp's $300 million 10-year A2/A-minus notes widened three basis points to an offer of 57 basis points over Treasuries.
The billion-plus plate of U.S. investment grade debt issuance on Wednesday did not damage market sentiment, traders said, and new deals thundered through with nary a snag.
"The (Treasury) market is up a little from where the deals came so they're just backing if off a little," one trader said. "I think that's all that says about the market."

For all the optimism in high-grades, junk traders said issues there commanded higher prices across the board despite the $2.5 billion in supply to hit the market between Wednesday and next Tuesday. Mutual fund flows are strong, they said, and some foresee a dearth of issuance during holidays.
Ryder TRS Inc's $175 million 144a 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced at par to yield 10 percent on Wednesday, were quoted at 101-1/4 bid, 101-3/4 offer at mid-session.
And Gorges/Quik-to-Fix Foods' $100 million 10-year 144a senior subordinated notes, priced on Thursday at par to yield 11-1/2 percent, were also quoted at 101-1/4 bid, 101-3/4 offer at mid-session.
Another dozen high-yield issues are expected to price between Thursday and Friday alone.
Turning to global issuance, Russia issued $1.0 billion five-year Eurobonds as 9-1/4s to yield 345 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve. The debt is rated Ba2/BB-minus.
